items.title: Spectral sequence subquotient and local lifting calculus
items.statement: In an abelian category use U+V=im(U direct-sum V -> X), U intersection V=their pullback, and inverse images as pullbacks. For V <= U <= X, (X/V)/(U/V) is canonically X/U; (U+V)/V is canonically U/(U intersection V). If U<=W, W intersection (U+V)=U+(W intersection V). Maps preserving numerator and denominator descend uniquely to quotients. A morphism to the image of f lifts through f after pullback along an epimorphism; equality can be checked after that epimorphism. All constructions are natural.
items.strategy: First derive normality directly, without an opposite-category supplier: for monic m the coimage projection is an isomorphism since ker m=0; the abelian comparison is an isomorphism, so m is a kernel of coker m. For epic e the image inclusion is an isomorphism since coker e=0; the same comparison identifies e with coker(ker e). The coimage projection is epic by cokernel uniqueness, the image inclusion monic by kernel uniqueness; hence every f factors epically onto its image and A/ker f is canonically im f. Pullbacks exist as kernels of f p_A-e p_B on the finite biproduct. If e is epic, this difference D is epic since D i_B=-e. If q kills the pullback projection alpha, then q p_A kills ker D, so normality of D gives v D=q p_A. Composing with i_B gives v e=0, hence v=0, and composing with i_A gives q=0. Thus alpha is epic: any difference of two arrows killed by alpha is zero. This proves the epic-pullback input locally. Factor f as its coimage epimorphism followed by image monomorphism using the abelian axiom; pull back the epimorphism to obtain the local lift. Define sums by finite biproduct images and intersections by kernels of difference maps; no infinite coproduct is used. The kernel of U -> X/V is U intersection V because V is the kernel of its cokernel (not because of a cokernel universal property). Its image is (U+V)/V: both maps are epimorphisms onto the same image after killing the V summand. Apply the coimage-to-image identification just proved. For V<=U, U/V -> X/V is monic by this calculation and X/U is its cokernel by the universal property, giving the nested quotient identity. For modularity, locally lift a map into W intersection (U+V) to u+v using the biproduct image epimorphism; since u factors through W, v does too. This proves inclusion in U+(W intersection V) after an epic cover; normality of the target subobject descends the inclusion. The reverse inclusion is immediate. Cokernel uniqueness proves quotient descent and naturality; epic cancellation proves equality. These finite local lifts require no choice axiom.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Abelian categories, Section 12.5

items.title: Increasing and decreasing filtration of an object
items.statement: An increasing filtration of A is specified subobjects F_p A <= F_{p+1} A for every integer p. Decreasing means F^{p+1} A <= F^p A; translation on the same object is F^p A=F_{-p} A. Morphisms preserve each indexed subobject.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Exhaustive separated bounded and finite filtration
items.statement: Exhaustive means the indicated union (supremum of subobjects) is A; separated means the indicated intersection is zero, only when these exist. Finite means F_a A=0 and F_b A=A for some a<b. A complex filtration is degreewise bounded if such a,b exist separately in each chain degree; uniformly bounded requires the same a,b in every degree. In modules these unions and intersections have their ordinary meanings. Completeness, when used for orientation, means A -> lim_p A/F_p A as p tends to minus infinity is an isomorphism; no unbounded convergence is asserted.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Associated graded object of a filtered object
items.statement: The associated graded is the indexed family gr^F_p A=coker(F_{p-1} A -> F_p A); for decreasing filtrations it is F^p A/F^{p+1} A. This is a family, not an assumed infinite direct sum.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Associated graded quotients are well defined subquotients
items.statement: The associated graded quotients exist as subquotients of A, independently up to unique compatible isomorphism of the representing inclusions.
items.strategy: Treat both conventions: form the cokernel of F_{p-1} -> F_p for an increasing filtration and of F^{p+1} -> F^p for a decreasing filtration. Compatible isomorphisms of either pair of inclusions induce inverse maps of cokernels by uniqueness.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Filtered chain complex
items.statement: A filtered chain complex (C,d,F) in an abelian category has an increasing filtration in each degree whose inclusions assemble into subcomplexes: d_n restricts F_p C_n -> F_p C_{n-1}.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Filtered chain map
items.statement: A filtered chain map f:C -> D is a chain map whose f_n restricts F_p C_n -> F_p D_n for every p,n.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: The associated graded of a filtered complex is a bigraded complex
items.statement:
Let $(C,d,F)$ be an increasingly filtered chain complex in an abelian category, and let $\pi_{p,n}:F_pC_n\to F_pC_n/F_{p-1}C_n$ be the quotient projections. The family $\operatorname{gr}^F_pC_{p+q}$ has the canonical differential $d^0_{p,q}$ uniquely characterized, for $n=p+q$, by
$d^0_{p,q}\pi_{p,n}=\pi_{p,n-1}(d_n|_{F_pC_n}).$
This differential has bidegree $(0,-1)$ and satisfies $(d^0)^2=0$. The family with this differential is the associated graded complex.
items.strategy: Apply quotient-complex descent to F_{p-1}C inside F_pC; explicitly specify its unique projection identity, then prove bidegree (0,-1) and square zero by epic cancellation.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Induced filtration on homology
items.statement: F_p H_n(C)=im(H_n(F_p C) -> H_n(C)), using the inclusion chain map. Factorization of F_{p-1} C -> C through F_p C shows these are an increasing filtration.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: The associated graded of filtered homology is a subquotient of chain level data
items.statement: Writing Z_n=ker d_n and D_n=im d_{n+1}, gr_p^F H_n(C) is canonically (F_p C_n intersection Z_n)/((F_{p-1} C_n intersection Z_n)+(F_p C_n intersection D_n)).
items.strategy: The image defining F_p H_n is the image of F_p C_n intersection Z_n in Z_n/D_n, hence ((F_p C_n intersection Z_n)+D_n)/D_n. Take the quotient by the previous filtration image, use the nested quotient rule, then the second quotient rule and modularity with F_{p-1} intersection Z_n <= F_p intersection Z_n.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: R cycles and r boundaries of an increasingly filtered complex
items.statement: Put n=p+q and A^r_{p,n}=F_p C_n intersection d_n^{-1}(F_{p-r} C_{n-1}) for r>=0; A^0_{p,n}=F_p C_n. For r>=1 define Z^r_{p,q}=A^r_{p,n} and B^r_{p,q}=A^{r-1}_{p-1,n}+d_{n+1}(A^{r-1}_{p+r-1,n+1}), as subobjects of F_p C_n. Separately set Z^0=F_p C_n and B^0=F_{p-1} C_n. The symbols B^r include lower-filtration approximate cycles, not just actual boundaries. For comparison with sources define bar-Z^r and bar-B^r as the images in gr_p C_n of A^r and d(A^{r-1}_{p+r-1,n+1}); for r=0 use gr_p and zero.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: R boundaries embed in r cycles
items.statement: B^r_{p,q} <= Z^r_{p,q} for every r>=0.
items.strategy: For r>=1 the first summand lies in F_{p-1} with differential in F_{p-r}; the second lies in F_p by its A^{r-1} bound and its differential is zero. The r=0 inclusion is the filtration inclusion.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: R page of the spectral sequence of a filtered complex
items.statement: Set E^r_{p,q}=Z^r_{p,q}/B^r_{p,q}. For r>=1 it is canonically bar-Z^r/bar-B^r inside the associated-graded model; E^0=gr_p C_{p+q}. The equality A^r_{p,n} intersection F_{p-1} C_n=A^{r-1}_{p-1,n} and the subquotient lemma justify the comparison. At fixed p,n and r<=k, finite windows F_{p+k}C/F_{p-k-1}C give the same r-page at that bidegree, by the displayed A and denominator bounds (the d targets and sources involved remain inside this window).

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: The filtered differential induces d r on the r page
items.statement: The differential induces d^r:E^r_{p,q} -> E^r_{p-r,q+r-1} by x -> d x.
items.strategy: For r>=1, d maps A^r into A^r at (p-r,n-1) since d squared is zero. For a in A^{r-1}_{p-1,n}, d a is in the target denominator term d(A^{r-1}_{p-1,n}); d kills the other denominator summand. Quotient descent gives a unique map. At r=0 use the already constructed associated-graded differential. Local representatives mean maps after epic pullback, never elements of an arbitrary abelian category.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: The rth differential has bidegree minus r r minus one
items.statement: The rth differential has bidegree (-r,r-1), total degree -1; the stable design ID is retained despite its misleading verbal suffix.
items.strategy: The target filtration index is p-r and the target total degree is p+q-1; subtract to obtain q+r-1.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: The rth differential squares to zero
items.statement: (d^r)^2=0 for all r>=0.
items.strategy: The composite precomposed with the epimorphism A^r -> E^r is induced by d squared, hence zero. Cancel that epimorphism.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: The next page is the homology of the current page
items.statement: There is a specified natural isomorphism alpha_r:H(E^r,d^r) -> E^{r+1} at every bidegree, for r>=0.
items.strategy: For r>=1 put K=A^r_{p,n}, L=A^{r-1}_{p-1,n}, J=d(A^{r-1}_{p+r-1,n+1}). A class killed by d^r has locally dx=a+db with a in A^{r-1}_{p-r-1,n-1} and b in A^{r-1}_{p-1,n}; then x-b belongs to A^{r+1}_{p,n}. Thus A^{r+1} maps epically onto ker d^r. Its kernel after quotienting by im d^r is A^r_{p-1,n}+d(A^r_{p+r,n+1}): the incoming image is d(A^r_{p+r,n+1}), J is contained therein, and intersection of A^{r+1} with L is A^r_{p-1,n}. Modularity gives exactly this denominator. The subquotient lemma turns the local lift computation into the canonical isomorphism E^{r+1} -> H(E^r); take its inverse as alpha_r. For r=0, cycles in F_p/F_{p-1} lift to A^1 and boundaries lift to d(F_p C_{n+1})+F_{p-1} C_n, yielding E^1 directly. Quotient uniqueness proves naturality.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: E zero is the associated graded complex
items.statement: E^0 with its differential is exactly the associated-graded complex in the stated quotient model.
items.strategy: Use Z^0=F_p, B^0=F_{p-1}, and the unique descended differential.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: E one is homology of the associated graded complex
items.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism $E^1_{p,q}\cong H_{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^F_pC)$, inverse to the specified initial next-page map. If $d(F_pC_n)\subseteq F_{p-1}C_{n-1}$ for all $p,n$, then $E^1_{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}_pC_{p+q}$ and $d^1$ is the map between these graded objects induced by $d$.
items.strategy: Apply the r=0 next-page calculation to the associated-graded complex. If d(F_p) lies in F_{p-1}, d^0 is zero and d^1 is induced by d between adjacent filtration quotients; this is a direct substitution into item 13.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Limiting cycles boundaries and e infinity
items.statement: For a filtered complex use the nested bar-B^r <= bar-B^{r+1} <= bar-Z^{r+1} <= bar-Z^r subobjects of E^0, rather than the unprojected B^r of item 10. Define bar-Z^infinity as their meet and bar-B^infinity as their join, only when these exist as subobjects; E^infinity is the quotient. In eventually stationary situations they are the eventual finite values. No unbounded abutment follows from this notation.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Homological spectral sequence
items.statement: A homological spectral sequence starting at a specified nonnegative r0 is a family E^r_{p,q}, maps d^r of bidegree (-r,r-1) with square zero, and specified isomorphisms alpha_r:H(E^r)->E^{r+1}. Homology is formed at each bidegree without infinite sums. First (third) quadrant means support p,q>=0 (p,q<=0); bounded means finitely many nonzero initial terms on every diagonal p+q=n.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Cohomological spectral sequence
items.statement: A cohomological spectral sequence in an abelian category has d_r:E_r^{p,q}->E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}, square zero, and specified next-page isomorphisms in that category. It corresponds to a homological one under (p,q)->(-p,-q).

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Morphism of spectral sequences
items.statement: A morphism from a declared page s consists of bidegree (0,0) maps f_r for r>=s, commuting with d_r and satisfying f_{r+1} alpha_r=alpha_r prime H(f_r). A map of abutments is extra compatible filtered data, not inherent in an abstract spectral-sequence map. An isomorphism on one whole page gives isomorphisms on every subsequent page: conjugate kernels and images by the page isomorphism and apply alpha at each step.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: A filtered chain map induces a morphism of spectral sequences
items.statement: Every filtered chain map induces a morphism of spectral sequences from page zero, respecting identities and composition. If its map on some page $s$ is an isomorphism in every bidegree, it is an isomorphism on every later page and on $E^\infty$ whenever the defining limiting subobjects exist.
items.strategy: The chain-map equation and filtration preservation take every A^r and denominator into its counterpart. Descend the maps, commute with d, and use the representative construction of alpha_r. Quotient uniqueness proves both functorial identities. In an eventually stable situation the same argument identifies the infinity maps; an isomorphism of one page remains an isomorphism at the stable page.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Spectral sequence stabilization at a bidegree
items.statement: Stabilization at (p,q) means all incoming and outgoing differentials there vanish for every r>=R, so alpha_r provides eventual identifications. An isomorphism of the underlying objects alone is insufficient. In the abstract case transport kernels and boundaries to nested subobjects of the initial page by successive inverse images under quotient maps; their eventual quotient is E^infinity.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Collapse at a page
items.statement: Collapse at E^s means every differential at every bidegree vanishes for all r>=s, and the transition data identify E^s with the stable page. A single zero differential or pointwise stabilization with unbounded R(p,q) is not collapse.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Degree reasons force stabilization in a bounded region
items.statement:
A bounded spectral sequence stabilizes at each bidegree. In particular first- and third-quadrant spectral sequences stabilize pointwise. If the initial support is globally finite, there is a uniform collapse page.

Here regular means eventual vanishing of the outgoing differential at each position, and coregular means eventual vanishing of the incoming differential. These conditions are respectively equivalent to eventual stationarity of the nested cycle and boundary subobjects in the initial page. In the homological convention, bounded below means each diagonal has support bounded below in its first coordinate; bounded above means support bounded above. Boundedness is equivalent to having both bounds. Bounded below implies regular; bounded above implies coregular. The cohomological versions follow by reversing both coordinates, so their named support directions are reversed.
items.strategy: Zeros persist under subquotients. At n=p+q the outgoing and incoming targets lie on diagonals n-1 and n+1 at filtration coordinates p-r and p+r. Each has finite support at the starting page, so choose an integer R beyond their finitely many differences from p. For first quadrant use R>max(p,q+1); third quadrant follows the analogous inequalities. A finite maximum suffices for finite global support, with no choice and no convergence inference.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Collapse from one column at page s ≥ 1 or one row at page s ≥ 2
items.statement: In the homological convention support in one column at E^s with s>=1 forces collapse there; support in one row at E^s with s>=2 forces collapse there. For cohomological indexing the same starting-page bounds apply.
items.strategy: Use the abstract spectral-sequence definitions to propagate zero support through successive homology subquotients. For r>=1 the filtration coordinate changes, so a single column forbids any differential; for r>=2 the complementary coordinate changes, so a single row forbids any differential. Reverse both coordinates for the cohomological case. At r=0 a column can carry d^0; at r=1 a row can carry d^1.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Abutment to a filtered object
items.statement: Abutment data to a filtered family H_n are specified identifications E^infinity_{p,q} -> F_p H_{p+q}/F_{p-1} H_{p+q}. On this page all asserted convergence uses finite filtrations in each degree; the associated graded is never identified with the unfiltered target without extra data.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Bounded filtered complex spectral sequence abuts to filtered homology
items.statement: If the filtration on every C_n is finite, its spectral sequence stabilizes and naturally abuts to H_n(C) with the image filtration F_p H_n(C). That filtration is finite, exhaustive and separated. No uniform bound in n is required.
items.strategy: Fix p,n. Choose r>=1 such that F_{p-r} C_{n-1}=0 and F_{p+r-1} C_{n+1}=C_{n+1}. The numerator A^r becomes F_p C_n intersection ker d_n; the first denominator becomes F_{p-1} C_n intersection ker d_n; and the second becomes F_p C_n intersection im d_{n+1}, using epic pullback for the image intersection. These formulas persist for larger r. Item 9 identifies the quotient with gr_p H_n. Bounds on C_n give zero and full homology-filtration endpoints. All maps come from chain-level maps, hence naturality. This is a degreewise finite proof in an arbitrary abelian category; no derived limits or exactness of infinite sums is assumed.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Edge homomorphisms of a first quadrant spectral sequence
items.statement: For a first-quadrant homological sequence from a page s>=2 with abutment filtration normalized F_{-1}H_n=0 and F_nH_n=H_n, define the edge maps E^s_{0,n} -> E^infinity_{0,n}=F_0H_n -> H_n and H_n -> H_n/F_{n-1}H_n=E^infinity_{n,0} -> E^s_{n,0}. The first composite need not be epic and the second need not be monic. The cohomological arrows are E_s^{n,0}->H^n and H^n->E_s^{0,n}.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Edge homomorphisms are natural
items.statement: The edge maps commute with compatible maps of spectral sequences and filtered abutments, in particular those induced by filtered chain maps satisfying the first-quadrant endpoint hypotheses.
items.strategy: All zero-axis incoming or outgoing arrows make the successive maps quotient maps or subobject inclusions. Their composites commute by the alpha compatibility; compose with the compatible filtration inclusions and quotient maps.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Extension problem of a convergent spectral sequence
items.statement: The extension problem is reconstructing H_n from its successive pieces gr_p H_n; the missing data are the extensions F_{p-1}H_n -> F_pH_n -> gr_p H_n. Neither collapse nor a list of pieces supplies splittings.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Abelian-group model for spectral-sequence computations
items.statement: Abelian groups and homomorphisms give an abelian category with kernels and images the ordinary subgroups and cokernels the coset quotients. In particular Z, Z/2, Z/4 and their finite products may be used for the explicit filtered complexes below; multiplication by 2 on Z is injective with cokernel Z/2.
items.strategy: Composition and identities are the underlying functions with domain/codomain tags. Pointwise addition makes each hom-set an abelian group and composition bilinear. The trivial group is zero; the cartesian product of two groups, with coordinate inclusions and projections, is also their coproduct via (a,b) -> f(a)+g(b). For f:G->H, ker f={g:f(g)=0} and im f={f(g)} are subgroups. On an abelian group H define h~k iff h-k lies in im f: reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow from subgroup closure, so the quotient set exists. Addition of classes is well-defined since differences add, and inverse is negation. Any homomorphism killing im f factors uniquely by [h]->u(h), giving the cokernel; the kernel universal property is restriction. Finally [g]->f(g) identifies G/ker f bijectively with im f, and its inverse preserves addition, proving the abelian axiom. This supplies Ab directly without the published all-small-limit/module route. The ordered-ring law makes 2z=0 imply z=0; the cokernel of 2 is the congruence quotient by 2Z, with class addition agreeing with the earlier modular-arithmetic construction. Z/2 and Z/4 use precisely those earlier operations; the finite computations below check their class maps explicitly. No choice of a representative function is used. A homomorphism preserves zero and negation because f(0)=f(0)+f(0) and f(x)+f(-x)=f(0). Division with remainder for the positive divisors 2 and 4 gives the unique residue representatives 0,1 and 0,1,2,3 respectively; these finite lists justify every class count and exponent comparison below.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Definition 12.5.1 (axiom checklist; model verified locally)

items.title: Isomorphic associated graded objects need not give isomorphic filtered objects
items.statement: The filtered groups Z/4 with 0<2Z/4<Z/4 and (Z/2)^2 with 0<(Z/2)x0<(Z/2)^2 have isomorphic associated-graded families but nonisomorphic underlying groups.
items.strategy: Compute both quotients by explicit reduction maps, each giving Z/2 in filtration indices 0 and 1. The first group has an element of order four and every element of the second is killed by two. This is a direct specialization of the extension ambiguity in Weibel after 5.2.12; no classification theorem or Ext machinery is used.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Collapse does not in general split the abutment
items.statement: Collapse does not in general split the filtered abutment.
items.strategy: Put the two groups of item 33 in chain degree zero with zero differential and their indicated filtrations. Every page differential vanishes; the abutments are the original groups. A splitting for Z/4 would give an isomorphism to (Z/2)^2, contradicted by element orders.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: The cohomological filtered complex construction
items.statement: For a cochain complex K with decreasing filtration F^p, set C_n=K^{-n}, F_p C_n=F^{-p} K^{-n}, d_n=d_K^{-n}. Then E_r^{p,q}(K)=E^r_{-p,-q}(C), d_r has bidegree (r,1-r), E_0=gr^p K^{p+q}, E_1=H^{p+q}(gr^p K), and for degreewise finite filtration E_infinity=gr^p H^{p+q}(K), naturally.
items.strategy: Substitute n=-m and p=-a in every cycle, boundary and differential formula. The chain equation is the cochain equation. The finite convergence theorem transfers with F^p H^m=F_{-p}H_{-m}(C). No sign enters this reversal of grading.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: Shifting a filtered complex reindexes its spectral sequence
items.statement: For integers a,b define D_n=C_{n-a}, d_D=d_C and G_p D_n=F_{p-b} C_{n-a}. Then E^r_{p,q}(D,G)=E^r_{p-b,q+b-a}(C,F) compatibly with differentials and next-page maps, and the same reindexing identifies finite filtered abutments. This is the explicitly sign-free degree translation, not the signed triangulated shift.
items.strategy: Substitute the two indices in A^r and B^r, and use the resulting identical quotient maps. Distinguish this translation from C[1] with its signed differential; no mapping-cone dependency is invoked.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: E infinity is the abutment object
items.statement: It is false that E^infinity is the abutment itself.
items.strategy: Use the Z/4 stalk filtration of item 33: its two graded pieces are Z/2, while H_0 has exponent four.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: E r plus one is literally equal to the homology of e r
items.statement: It is false that literal equality E^{r+1}=H(E^r) is required by the definition.
items.strategy: Take a spectral sequence with zero differential supported at (0,0) and use distinct tagged copies of Z/2 on successive pages, with the obvious group isomorphisms as alpha. Each is a legitimate sequence; literal set equality fails.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra

items.title: A spectral sequence collapses when one differential is zero
items.statement: It is false that d^s=0 alone implies collapse at E^s.
items.strategy: In Ab let C_2=Z generated by x, C_1=Z generated by y, dx=y. Give x filtration 2 and y filtration 0. Then E^0 and E^1 have Z at (2,0) and (0,1), with d^0=d^1=0, but d^2 is the identity and E^3=0.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5

items.title: Collapse solves all extension problems
items.statement: It is false that collapse solves all extension problems.
items.strategy: Build the degree-zero stalk on the filtered group 0 subset {0,2} subset Z/4. Compute every page as the two Z/2 graded pieces with zero differentials, identify the abutment as filtered Z/4, and check directly that the quotient to Z/2 has no additive section.

items.title: The filtration on homology is h n of the filtered subcomplex
items.statement: It is false that F_p H_n(C) is H_n(F_p C).
items.strategy: Use C_1=Z -> C_0=Z with identity differential and F_0 C the degree-zero subcomplex, F_1 C=C, F_{-1}=0. H_0(F_0 C)=Z but H_0(C)=0 and its induced filtration is zero.

items.title: E zero and e one page conventions are universal across sources
items.statement: It is false that E^0/E^1 notation is universal across sources.
items.strategy:
Distinguish two actual construction conventions rather than merely deleting a page. Vitolo, On different geometric formulations of Lagrangian formalism, corrected author version, Appendix B p33, initializes the generic derived-couple iteration with its input E object as E_0 and H(E) as E_1. Weibel Example 5.9.3 and Theorem 5.9.4, printed pp155–156, label the initial homology exact couple of a filtered complex E^1=H(gr C). Thus applying Vitolo's generic iteration to that same homology exact couple yields a generic page F_0=H(gr C), with F_n corresponding to the filtration-normalized E^(n+1). This compares actual initial page labels, not only coordinate names. Do not claim Vitolo's separately normalized filtered-complex Theorem8.1 disagrees with Weibel: it too adds gr C at E_0. The warning is that a construction's numbering must be specified; neither universal disagreement among authors nor a convention calling gr C page1 is asserted.

Give the complete local example using only the preceding Ab model. Let C_1=C_0=Z, let d:C_1->C_0 be the identity, and let all other groups be zero. Set F_p C=0 for p<0 and F_p C=C for p>=0. The associated graded is concentrated at filtration degree0 and is this nonzero two-term complex, so the library's E^0 is nonzero. Its homology vanishes in both degrees: ker(id)=0 and coker(id)=0. Hence E^1=0, and every subsequent page is zero by its specified homology transition. Every filtered piece and every associated-graded quotient also has zero homology. Consequently the homology exact-couple triangle is just 0->0->0->0. For completeness, an exact couple is a triangle D->D->E->D whose image equals the next kernel at each vertex, with differential on E the composite E->D->E. Here all maps, kernels, images and quotients are zero, so exactness and every derived zero triangle are checked directly. No general exact-couple construction theorem is consumed. Under the generic iteration convention its initial page F_0 is zero and every F_n remains zero. Under filtration normalization the same initial homology-couple term is E^1=0, whereas E^0 is the nonzero identity complex. This supplies a concrete distinction between the two page0 objects and the dictionary F_n=E^(n+1) on the common part.

The generic convention is for differential objects, not automatically the library's fixed bigraded definition: after shifting r to r+1 the old homological differential degree is (-(r+1),r), not (-r,r-1). State this accompanying degree shift if retaining the old coordinates. In the displayed zero tail every differential is zero, so its grading causes no extra premise. Merely removing E^0 while retaining E^1 as page1 would not prove the claimed numbering distinction.

Romyar Sharifi, Homological Algebra
Raffaele Vitolo, On different geometric formulations of Lagrangian formalism (corrected author version), Appendix B p33; filtered normalization pp34–35

items.title: The two step filtration and its spectral sequence
items.statement: For C_1=Z -> C_0=Z with differential multiplication by 2, let F_0 C be the degree-zero stalk, F_1 C=C, F_{-1}=0. Compute E^0, E^1, d^1, E^2 and the induced filtration on homology.
items.strategy: E^0=E^1 has Z at (1,0) and (0,0); d^0=0 and d^1 is multiplication by 2. E^2 has Z/2 at (0,0) only, all later differentials vanish, H_1=0 and H_0=Z/2.

items.title: A filtered complex collapsing at e one
items.statement: A trivially filtered two-term complex Z --2--> Z collapses at E^1.
items.strategy: Use F_p C=0 for p<0 and C for p>=0. Only column zero occurs. d^0=2, so E^1 has Z/2 at (0,0), all later differentials are zero, and the homology filtration is trivial.

items.title: A nonzero d two differential in a small filtered complex
items.statement: A finite filtered complex has d^0=d^1=0 but nonzero d^2.
items.strategy: Take C_2=Z x, C_1=Z y, dx=y, filtration levels 2 and 0. The only E^2 terms are Z at (2,0) and (0,1); d^2(x)=y is an isomorphism, so E^3=0 and the filtered homology is zero.

items.title: Edge maps from a first quadrant spectral sequence
items.statement: Compute the two edge maps for the two-step filtered complex Z --2--> Z.
items.strategy: Use the first example but repeat its construction here. On E^2 only E^2_{0,0}=Z/2 survives. In degree zero both edge composites are the identity of H_0=Z/2. In every positive degree the edge maps have zero source or target, with H_n=0.

items.title: Two filtered abelian groups with the same associated graded
items.statement: Explicitly compare the two associated-graded families of Z/4 and (Z/2)^2.
items.strategy: Write F_0=2Z/4 and (Z/2)x0 respectively, F_1 the whole group and F_{-1}=0. Use the declared modulo-n and componentwise product operations to verify the displayed quotient maps are additive bijections; exponent distinguishes the whole groups.

items.title: Collapse with a nonsplit extension problem
items.statement: A collapsed spectral sequence can have a nonsplit extension in its abutment.
items.strategy: Use the Z/4 stalk with F_0=2Z/4. Substitute its zero differential into the declared filtered-cycle, boundary, page, and page-differential formulas to compute the collapse locally. A section of reduction modulo two would send the nonzero element of Z/2 to an odd class killed by two, which is impossible in Z/4.

items.title: The cohomological reindexing of a homological spectral sequence
items.statement: Reindex a nonzero homological d^2 as a cohomological d_2.
items.strategy: For the identity complex C_2 -> C_1 with filtration levels 2 and 0, put K^{-2}=Z, K^{-1}=Z, decreasing jumps -2 and 0. Its nonzero d_2 goes from (-2,0) to (0,-1), bidegree (2,-1), and the next page vanishes.
